prompt: Why does Newton's method double the number of correct digits at each step near a simple root?
answer: Taylor's theorem at the current point gives 0 = f(x_k) + f'(x_k)(r - x_k) + f''(xi)(r - x_k)^2 / 2. Newton keeps only the linear part, so the new error is r - x_{k+1} = -f''(xi) / (2 f'(x_k)) times (r - x_k)^2: proportional to the square of the old error. An error of 10^-k becomes about 10^-2k.
